newsitem.title: UK: Mideast/west VLCC trade to fall, Asia to rise - repo.
newsitem.headline: Mideast/west VLCC trade to fall, Asia to rise - repo.

text.p: Very large crude carriers (VLCCs) will depend increasingly on trade from the Middle East to Asia rather than to the West as Western demand for Gulf oil declines, brokers Simpson, Spence & Young (SSY) said in a report on Thursday.
The report said an overall decline in crude shipments to markets west of Suez "has been due to the emergence in the 1990s of greater short-haul supplies from both sides of the Atlantic."
This had led to a fall in imports of Middle Eastern crude by the U.S. and European Union countries from 4.73 million barrels per day (bpd) in 1995 to 4.61 million last year.

SSY said data for January-September 1996 showed that Middle Eastern crude deliveries to the EU declined substantially, by some 120,000 bpd to 3.13 million bpd, while additional supplies came from short-haul sources, especially the former Soviet Union despite lower output from there for the ninth consecutive year.
While less Middle East crude was flowing west, more was going east, especially to South Korea, where Gulf imports rose by 170,000 bpd or 13 percent last year.
"Lower demand for Middle East crude in the West, amid rising short-haul supplies in the Atlantic, implies lower tonne-mile employment for large tankers on AG (Middle East)-West trades.
"This is expected to continue as supplies from Latin America and the North Sea are set to increase over the next decade," SSY said.

"In addition, an eventual full-scale resumption of oil exports from Iraq when the UN embargo is lifted would raise availability of Iraqi oil in the East Med, further dampening the demand for large tankers to Atlantic markets.
"Until these short-haul crude supplies in the West decline, this will make VLCC employment increasingly reliant on AG-Eastbound trades and on loadings outside the Middle East."
